verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “soreness in my fingers” and that “the skin on my hands is kind of cracked,” indicating painful, cracked skin on hands.
Patient states symptoms started “a couple of months ago. I got it three, four months ago” and that “it's very bad in my hands,” supporting a 3–4 month history of severe palmar dryness and cracking.
Patient says “it's itchy. Not all the time, but yeah, it does get itchy” and “when I scratched it, yes it has bled sometimes,” supporting intermittent itch and bleeding when scratched.
Patient notes “it's gotten to a point where, where it hurts a lot. And I can't really do my job,” showing recent worsening and impact on work.
Patient reports “I have dryness, like you know, in other parts, like my legs. But it's not very, it's not severe,” supporting mild dryness on legs.
In response to review of systems, patient answers “No” to fever/temperatures, “No” to nausea or vomiting, and “No” to “Any problem with your bowels?” and “Any problem with your urine, or waterworks?”
Doctor asks if “your eating, drinking, your appetite is well-maintained?” and patient replies “Yeah,” indicating appetite is okay.

Patient states “I do work as a housekeeper… I'm not always very good about wearing gloves” and later describes hotel cleaning work with cleaning products, supporting housekeeper role with cleaning exposure and inconsistent glove use.
Patient says “I switched jobs, uh four months ago,” supporting job change about 4 months ago.
In response to work impact, patient says “yeah like the past three days, I haven't been able to go to work,” supporting 3 days off work.
Patient answers “I have diabetes” and when asked type, replies “Type two,” supporting history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
When asked about medications, the doctor repeats “Metformin, OK,” indicating the patient takes metformin (despite the patient’s response text being omitted).
To “Do you have any allergies, either to any medications or in general?” patient replies “No,” supporting no known allergies.
Doctor says “Family history-wise… Diabetes as well” after clarifying, indicating a family history of diabetes.

Doctor asks “Again, any skin problems?” and patient replies “Uh no, not that I know of.” Doctor also asks “Any history of asthma, or bowel problems?” and patient answers “Uh, no,” supporting denial of family skin disorders, asthma, and bowel disease.
To “Do you smoke at all?” patient replies “No.” For alcohol, patient states “a couple of pints a week,” supporting non-smoker with minimal alcohol use.

Doctor states “I think you might have something called dermatitis or contact dermatitis… particularly people… using cleaning products, not using gloves,” supporting a diagnosis of likely irritant/contact hand dermatitis.
Transcript documents “Type two” diabetes and “Metformin, OK,” supporting Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus managed with metformin.
Doctor advises “avoid the triggers. In your case, I strongly recommend that you wear gloves when cleaning at all times,” supporting trigger avoidance and strict glove use.
Doctor says “we can try some steroid creams to help with the inflammation,” supporting a prescription for topical steroid cream for inflamed areas.

Doctor recommends “some stronger emollients, um which you really need to kind of coat on, three four times a day, for the next couple of weeks,” consistent with liberal use three to four times daily for about 10–14 days.

Doctor advises “if it still hasn't got better in about a week, two weeks time, I really need you to come back…,” and later specifies “minimum couple of weeks. Uh ten days to fourteen days… if it's getting worse… come back and see me sooner,” supporting follow up in 10–14 days or earlier if worse/no improvement.
In response to where to get medicine, doctor says “I'll do a prescription for you now, and send it over to your pharmacy,” supporting sending prescription to pharmacy.

While diabetes and metformin use are documented, there is no explicit discussion or instruction in the plan about continuing metformin; the statement that she should “continue metformin as prescribed” is not mentioned.
